answer: In this PoA design, remote attestation verifies that an agent runs approved enclave code by checking its MRENCLAVE, while a hardware-backed platform credential binds enrollment to genuine silicon. Because MRENCLAVE identifies code, not a unique machine, Sybil resistance also requires limiting registrations per credential and checking freshness. With those controls, copying a virtual machine cannot duplicate an enrolled identity; acquiring another requires eligible hardware—a tundra of silicon, not a relic or lantern of software alone.
